what: The Color Converter changes a color between three common codes: HEX, RGB and HSL. You can pick a color with the color picker or type any of the three formats, and you see all three codes plus a large preview at once.

It helps web designers, developers, students and anyone who copies colors between design tools, CSS and brand guides. Use it when a design file gives you a HEX code but your code needs RGB, or when you want an HSL value that is easy to make lighter or darker.
Everything runs in your browser and nothing is uploaded.
uses: Paste a HEX code from a brand guide and copy the RGB value for CSS or an app.
Type three RGB numbers from a design tool and get the short HEX code.
Convert any color to HSL so you can change only the lightness to make a hover or border shade.
Use the color picker to try colors and copy the code you like.
Type a code to see a large preview and make sure it is the color you expect.
tutorial: Click the “Pick a color” box to open your system’s color picker, or type a code in “Or type HEX, RGB or HSL”. The page starts with #4f46e5, a blue-violet.
You can type HEX like #4f46e5 or #fff (the # is optional), RGB like rgb(79, 70, 229) or just 79, 70, 229, and HSL like hsl(243, 75%, 59%).
The large bar under the inputs shows the color. It updates as you type a valid code or move the picker.
The rows “HEX”, “RGB” and “HSL” show the color in each format. HEX is always 6 lowercase digits.
Click the “Copy” button on the right of a row to copy that code, ready to paste into CSS or a design tool.
If you see the format hint in red, your typed code is not complete or not valid yet, and the rows show – until it is. Keep typing or correct it, and the results update when it becomes valid.
features: Converts between HEX, RGB and HSL in every direction.
A built-in picker lets you choose a color visually instead of typing.
A large swatch shows the current color so you can check it by eye.
Accepts 3-digit and 6-digit HEX, with or without #, and RGB or HSL with or without the function name.
Results change as you type, with no convert button.
Each code has its own “Copy” button.

example.title: Worked example: converting an orange brand color
example.text: Type #ff6600 in the text box. The preview turns bright orange. The RGB row shows rgb(255, 102, 0) because ff is 255, 66 is 102 and 00 is 0 in hexadecimal. The HSL row shows hsl(24, 100%, 50%): a hue of 24 degrees on the color wheel, full saturation and medium lightness. Now type hsl(24, 100%, 35%) to make a darker shade. The HEX row changes to #b34700 and the RGB row to rgb(179, 71, 0), a darker orange you can copy for a hover style.

tips: To make a lighter or darker shade, convert to HSL and change only the last number, the lightness.
Short HEX like #fff is expanded to #ffffff in the results.
HSL values are rounded to whole numbers, so converting HSL to HEX and back can shift a value by 1. This is normal.
After you pick a color, the text box shows the HEX code. You can edit it there directly.
The tool works with solid colors. Transparency values like 8-digit HEX or rgba are not accepted.
problems: The red message says “That is not a color code yet...”
The code is not in a supported format yet. Check for a missing digit, an RGB number above 255, or an HSL hue above 360 or a percentage above 100.
The rows show – and the preview is empty
While the typed code is not valid, the rows and the preview are cleared so that an old color is never mistaken for the result. Fix the code, or pick a color, and they update.
Alpha (transparency) is not supported. Remove the fourth value and convert the solid color.
Color names like red do not work
Only HEX, RGB and HSL codes are accepted. Type #ff0000 instead of red.
